content:
Good morning.

Good morning. Thank you.

Isn't it great to be in San Francisco?

So, we have so much great stuff for you today that we may even have to take a stretch break in the middle here.

A lot of good stuff. I hope you love it uh as much as we do. So, there are about 3800 of us here today. Uh we're a little over 1% of the registered Apple developers. There's over 300,000 now and that number has tripled since the num- since the introduction of Mac OS 10. Uh not only carbon and cocoa developers but a ton of Unix developers have joined us, a lot of Java developers as well. So, we're really excited about this.

I want to start with some updates and then we'll get into the meat of today's presentation. First, I want to talk about Airport Extreme. Uh Airport Extreme is our 54 megabit per second airport product that's based on the industry standard 802.11g. And the standard was not yet ratified when we started shipping in January. We were the first to ship this, but it was ratified uh a little over a week ago. And one week after it was ratified, we had an airport soft- software update on the net for base stations and cards to bring them totally in compliance with the final ratified spec. We are 1000% sure that 802.11g is the successor to 802.11b. It's totally backwards compatible. And as I mentioned, Apple was the first to ship 802.11g in our industry just as we were the first to ship uh 802.11 wireless networking in computers years ago. And I'm pleased to report that since we started shipping 802.11g in January, we've shipped over 300,000 802.11g products. So that's an update on Airport Extreme. We couldn't be happier with the progress. Next, I want to give you an update on our retail stores. Uh this is off the charts. Uh it's been 25 months since we opened our first store. We now have 58 stores open. Since we've opened them, we've had over 17 million visitors to our stores. 17 million. This is our store in New York. It's one of the coolest stores in New York. If you've ever been there, I'd worth a visit if you're in the city. It's wonderful. This is our largest store in Los Angeles in the Grove Shopping Center and again shows how much software we carry in our stores. We love to carry your software. And among the many stores we're going to be opening in the next year, we're opening three really great stores, one in Chicago, one in San Francisco and one in Tokyo. We're opening Chicago this coming weekend.

And this is a photo from last week.

We'll open San Francisco uh next spring. But uh this is a rendering. I wish it was as easy to build them. Uh and uh this is at the end of Stockton Street viewed from Market Street. This is what it will look like, only a few blocks from where we are sitting here right now. And in Tokyo, we are opening a store.

It's going to be great. In Tokyo, we are opening a store on the Ginza uh which is the number one shopping street in the world and we're opening it early next year and again this is a rendering of what it will be.

So, we've had 17 million visitors and counting. We love to sell your software and hardware accessory products. So keep keep feeding them to us and we can't wait to put them in our stores. So that's an update on our retail stores. Next, iPod. iPod, again, we couldn't be happier with. We just introduced our third generation iPod. Our competitors haven't even caught up with our first generation yet. We're in our third and it is amazing. Uh it is as light as two CDs in their jewel cases. It is as thin as two CD jewel cases back to back. It has a dock so that charging and sinking is even more convenient than before. And I've got a great milestone today. Today's an auspicious day because later on today we will ship our 1 millionth iPod.

So, another great product for music of course, iTunes 4. And the greatest feature of iTunes 4 is of course the iTunes Music Store. Being an auspicious day today, it was eight weeks ago today that we launched the iTunes Music Store, only eight weeks ago and I'm pleased to report that in the first eight weeks, we've sold over 5 million songs online.

We crossed the 5 million mark this last Saturday and we again are thrilled. Now, we ran an ad campaign about uh about the iTunes Music Store and you know when you run an ad campaign if it's really working, if it if it resonates with the culture, if people start to parody it. And uh it wasn't very long before that happened and uh when I saw this on on TV.

So, doesn't get any better than that. Okay, so that's the iTunes Music Store. Next, I want to give you an update on Safari. As you know, Safari is the fastest browser on the Mac and we think it's the best browser on any platform. We've had over 5 million downloads of the Safari beta software that we released in January and it's a phenomenal browser. We were able over the course of the beta period to add tab browsing. I think we've got the slickest implementation of tab browsing ever done. It's been six months that we've had the beta software out there. You guys have given us a phenomenal number of comments. We've incorporated as many as we could in and I think we've got an incredibly solid browser now. And so today we are declaring Safari 1.0.

We're releasing it on the web in a few hours. You can download your copy and we're also fulfilling a request we've had from so many of you that want to embed Safari functionality in your apps by just calling a few carbon or cocoa APIs. Today we're releasing a Safari SDK to all of you as well.

So, that's Safari and that concludes my updates. Now let's get right into it. I want to talk about Mac OS 10. Mac OS 10 is doing really, really well. Let me show you. Over the last two years, we've gone from about a half a million active users to 7 million active users of Mac OS 10. And look at the slope of that curve. It's going up. We have 6,000 native Mac OS 10 apps. And again, let's take a look at the slope of this curve over the last two years starting with under 1000. It's accelerating. And this is obviously these two are linked. And so we are over the crest of the hill of the Mac OS 10 transition and we'll finish it up this year. And all I can say for all these apps is thank you. I know this has been a lot of work for some of you as any major OS transition is and you guys have really come through and we are just about through with this and we've got a kickass OS. So thank you.

But today, for all of us in this room, all the developers, Jaguar is over.

Because today we're going to preview Panther for you. The next major release of Mac OS 10, version 10.3. Its name is Panther and it's the fourth major release of Mac OS 10 following Cheetah, Puma and Jaguar. In Panther, there are over 100 major new features. We're not going to have time to go over all of them today, but I want to cover a few of them with you and I think you'll agree it's a stunning release. First, let's start off with Unix. As you know, Mac OS 10 is Unix based and as you also know, Mac OS 10 is now the most popular Unix in the world. The most popular Unix in the world. And we've enhanced it for Panther. We got a lot of cool new features. X11 is bundled in, NFS file locking, much faster Unix file system, much more robust Kerberos, Free BSD 5.0, IPv6 and a lot of popular Unix APIs that you guys have asked for. All of that and a lot more Unix stuff is in Panther. Now, in addition to Unix though, we support the other guys too. We want to help our customers work in heterogeneous networks and we've added a lot of stuff for Windows operability. We're shipping the latest version of Samba that just came out. We're the first folks to ship that I believe so that you can now browse SMB servers dynamically right in the finder, SMB printing, you can put your home directories on SMB servers. We're shipping a new IPsec based VPN, which is the new standard for VPN adopted by Cisco and Microsoft and us and a lot deeper active directory integration. So, a lot of stuff with Windows interoperability. Now let's get into some of the cooler stuff. Panther has a brand new finder.

Now, you might say, well wait a minute, what was wrong with the old finder? Well, the old finder was computer centric. When we really were honest with ourselves, we had to admit it. We did as best as we could, but we didn't quite get across the goal line. It was computer centric. What do I mean by that? Well, this is column view in the old finder, the Jaguar finder and that's my stuff right there, right? That's my stuff. Four levels down. How could I be the most important thing if I'm four levels down? And I need stuff at other levels and it's just very confusing. So, we want to replace this computer centric finder with a user centric finder. Well, how do we do that? Well, we start off by learning from some of the other interfaces we've built over the last few years and we said let's put all the stuff you want including stuff you want to drag in in one column and put it on the left and that's what we've done. All your storage, your removable storage, your iDisk, your home directory, any folders you want in one column. And let's put that on the left of a window. This might look a little bit like playlists in iTunes or photo albums in iPhoto. That's because it is. And you click on one of these things and boom, your stuff is right there. So here's my home, here's my applications, here's my documents. I can look at these things in column view, list view or icon view and have my stuff right there. Boom. And I can drag any folders I want right into that left column. It's really, really simple. Now, we've done more. We've added fast searching. So you can now search for files really fast and find them. We've added a thing called the action button. We found a lot of our users never found some of the cool things they could do. Some of them didn't even find get info. And so we pulled all that stuff under a button that's contextually sensitive. You push it, it'll show you exactly what you can do with a document or folder that you have selected. We've added labels. We got a lot of requests for labels. They're in there. As I mentioned earlier, we have dynamic network browsing. So you can dynamically search for Unix servers, for Windows servers, for any servers right from the finder. We've got new open and save panels that reflect this more user centric point of view, much cleaner. And probably the best way is for me to show this to you now.

So, the new finder. Here we go. You see the left column right here? I can just click down it and see all my stuff. And uh I can go ahead and go into icon view again. Just bop around and see all of my stuff very easy. And I can shrink the window. There's a lot of fit and finish on this so you'll notice the icons on the left shrink, right? Just like this. Don't scroll till they have to. And I can drag stuff in. I can drag a folder I want anywhere in here if I want to, just put it right there. And I click on that and I see its contents. If I'm tired of it, I just drag it out and it poofs. Okay. I can eject DVDs right from here with a roll over right like this so I don't even have to go to an eject button. And I can go on the network and see my servers right here and browse them dynamically. Now, let me go to my documents folder and uh oh maybe uh where is it? Boom boom boom. I can go pick the action menu and again, I can label something right like this. And boom, that's all it does. All it takes to set a label. It's very, very simple. And I've got fast search. So I'm in my home directory now. I can search all my my hard disks or just my home directory or window it down to whatever I want. I'm going to look for all the Xserve uh documents in my home directory just by typing Xserve. So the minute I start to type,

I can find all the iMac documents. Boom. Or eMac documents or PowerBook documents. Boom. It's that fast. It's really, really cool. And so that's a brief overview of the new finder and uh I think you're going to like it a lot. We've got it's user centric. We've got fast searching. We've got the action button to pull together a lot of commands that people have never found, labels, dynamic network browsing and new open and save panels that reflect the new user centric sensibility. So this is the new finder and I think uh it's going to serve us well. I think we finally got there on the finder with something that's the best the world's ever seen. Next is iDisk. We've enhanced iDisk significantly for Panther. Uh iDisk as you know is for our .Mac customers, the hundreds of thousands of people that have signed up for .Mac and iDisk has been a place where you can manually upload files to the .Mac server and manually download them. Well, that's all changing in Panther because in Panther we're automatically syncing the files. And what that means is is that stuff that's on your iDisk will automatically sync with our servers on .Mac in both directions. And it does it in the background. So what it really means is your iDisk becomes basically a local folder that syncs. You don't put stuff in your iDisk to send it up to .Mac. You leave it in your iDisk. You can leave a document in your iDisk, open it up, modify it, close it and the minute you close it, it will sync back up to .Mac in the background automatically. So you can just leave stuff in your iDisk. And this is pretty cool. It's a great way to back stuff up. But in addition to that, it really shines when you have untethered portables. You can be out in the field not connected to a network, change a document in your iDisk. The minute you're connected to a network whether you walk into an airport, a base station or you hook back up to a terrestrial net, boom, that document that's changed will automatically sync with .Mac. It's really nice and that is the new iDisk in Panther. Next up, we have a new feature called Exposé. What is Exposé? Well, we've made it so wonderful to use multiple apps at once that people do, right? The operating system is so bulletproof that if an app crashes it doesn't crash the system and we have such beautiful uh multitasking that you can have, you know, seven, eight, nine, 10 apps open at once. I'm sure most of you do. So you've got Photoshop shop open and you're working on a bunch of Photoshop images. You've got mail open, you've got your browser open, you've got your address book open and what do you end up with this? Right? We've all been there. We all are there several times a day and you want to find that one window you're looking for. How do you do it? All you want is to bring the one window you want to the front. So you move everything out of the way. You're like a you're on a scavenger hunt. Well, we figured out how to solve this in a wonderful way. Let me show you now.
